RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

An all-male panel is not definitive proof of discrimination, though research indicates demographic homogeneity can heighten unconscious bias. However, departments often legitimately weigh specific curricular needs, subfield alignment, or industry backgrounds over traditional publication counts. 

Before raising gender composition, follow up cordially on your feedback request. Check the university’s HR policies: many public institutions mandate gender-balanced panels, which would provide clear procedural grounds to inquire or appeal. If no policy was breached, raising bias directly without evidence risks damaging professional relationships and future prospects. Only pursue the issue formally through an ombudsperson or union representative if the university violated hiring regulations or if the forthcoming written feedback reveals clear irregularities.
